newsitem.title: USA: Ahmanson sees "minimal" layoffs in merger.
newsitem.headline: Ahmanson sees "minimal" layoffs in merger.

text.p: H.F. Ahmanson and Co, which launched a hostile $6.2 billion bid for Great Western Financial Corp, said layoffs would be "minimal" with such a merger if Great Western implemented hiring restraints.

"If Great Western will take the same prudent actions Ahmanson has already taken to limit employee dislocation, it can ensure that layoffs of Great Western employees would be minimal -- far less than has occurred in other major banking transactions," Charles Rinehart, chief executive officer of Ahmanson, said in a letter to Great Western's board on Friday.

The letter was an apparent response to a memo circulated to Great Western employees earlier this week by chief executive officer John Maher, who expressed his personal outrage at statements by Ahmanson indicating that all job losses related to the merger would be targeted at Great Western employees. Analysts estimate 2,500 jobs would be cut.

A source close to Great Western said job cuts would be far below that number. The source said when Ahmanson made the bid on February 17, it asked Great Western to implement a policy of hiring only on a basis of necessity, which Ahmanson has done.
Ahmanson said it would make layoff decisions based on merit but reiterated its commitment to Ahmanson employees.
"The combination of the significant reductions resulting from attrition and these increased staffing needs should reduce actual layoffs to a minimal number," the letter said.

"If we drew attention by being candid where other acquirors are not, we are prepared to live with it," Rinehart wrote. "Disproportionate treatment of employees occurs -- as a reality -- in virtually every merger and would occur if Great Western were acquired by a third party and any suggestion to the contrary is both inaccurate and creates misleading expectations for the Great Western employees."
